'''Sijue Wu''' ({{zh|s=邬似珏|p=Wū Sìjué}}; born May 15, 1964) is a [[Chinese American]] mathematician who works as the Robert W. and Lynne H. Browne Professor of Mathematics at the [[University of Michigan]]. Her research involves the mathematics of [[water wave]]s.<ref name="mactutor">{{MacTutor|title=Sijue Wu|id=Wu}}</ref><ref name="asc">{{citation|url=https://www.agnesscott.edu/lriddle/women/wu.htm|title=Sijue Wu|work=Biographies of Women Mathematicians|first=Larry|last=Riddle|publisher=[[Agnes Scott College]]|date=January 10, 2014|access-date=2015-10-22}}.</ref>

==Education and career==
Wu earned bachelor's and master's degrees in 1983 and 1986 from [[Peking University]].<ref name="mactutor"/><ref name="asc"/> She completed her doctorate in 1990 from [[Yale University]], under the supervision of [[Ronald Coifman]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=39115}}.</ref> After a temporary instructorship at [[New York University]], she became an assistant professor at [[Northwestern University]]. She moved in 1996 to the [[University of Iowa]] and again to the [[University of Maryland, College Park]] in 1998. She became the Browne Professor at the [[University of Michigan]] in 2008.<ref name="mactutor"/>

==Awards and honors==
A 1997 paper by Wu in ''[[Inventiones Mathematicae]]'', "Well-posedness in Sobolev spaces of the full water wave problem in 2-D", was the subject of a featured review in ''[[Mathematical Reviews]]''.<ref>{{citation
 | last = Wu | first = Sijue
 | doi = 10.1007/s002220050177
 | issue = 1
 | journal = Inventiones Mathematicae
 | mr = 1471885
 | pages = 39–72
 | title = Well-posedness in Sobolev spaces of the full water wave problem in 2-D
 | volume = 130
 | year = 1997| bibcode = 1997InMat.130...39W
 | s2cid = 126485710
 }}.</ref>

Wu was an [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 2002, speaking on [[partial differential equation]]s.<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByLastname.php|title=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers since 1897|publisher=[[International Mathematical Union]]|access-date=2015-10-22}}.</ref>

She won the [[Ruth Lyttle Satter Prize in Mathematics]]<ref name="satter">{{citation|url=http://www.ams.org/notices/200104/comm-satter.pdf|title=2001 Satter Prize|journal=[[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]]|date=April 2001|pages=411–412|volume=48|issue=4}}.</ref> and the silver [[Morningside Medal]] in 2001, and the gold Morningside Medal in 2010, becoming the first female mathematician to win the gold medal.<ref name="asc"/> She was elected to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2022.<ref>{{citation |title=American Academy of Arts & Sciences Announces New Members Elected in 2022 |url=https://www.amacad.org/news/2022-member-announcement |access-date=2022-05-22 |website=American Academy of Arts & Sciences |date=April 28, 2022 |language=en}}</ref>
